STATE OF THE TREE YOU INHERIT (verified live before this launch — do not re-litigate it, build against it):

1. ARCHITECTURE surface is DONE and frozen to you: IEnvironment.GetBaseDirectory() exists and its doc states the trailing-separator guarantee; EnvironmentAdapter.GetBaseDirectory() is the throwing stub (NotSupportedException, EnvironmentAdapter.cs:49) YOU fill; FakeEnvironment has the _baseDirectory field, the ctor param, and the Create(..., baseDirectory: null) seed defaulting to home.

2. TDD is DONE and frozen to you. Five acceptance facts exist: BaseDirectoryAccessorTests.GetBaseDirectory_ReturnsANonEmptyPathToADirectoryThatExists, and BaseDirectorySeparatorTests {RealBaseDirectory_EndsWithADirectorySeparator, FakeBaseDirectory_WhenSeededWithoutATrailingSeparator_AppendsExactlyOne, FakeBaseDirectory_WhenSeededAlreadyTerminated_ReturnsItUnchangedWithExactlyOneSeparator, FakeBaseDirectory_OnTheDefaultHomeFallbackPath_EndsWithADirectorySeparator}. Current state on this macOS host: Failed 4, Passed 1. The ONE passing fact is the already-terminated no-double guard — it is GREEN BY DESIGN under contract Decision 6 (Tim waived RED-first for exactly that fact because a throwing fake stub leaves _baseDirectory unread and fails analyzer S4487, which may not be suppressed). Do NOT try to make it red, do NOT touch it, and do NOT stub the fake to throw. Your job is to keep it green while turning the other four green.

3. PolkitPolicyIntegrityTests has ALREADY been rewritten by TDD to read Path.Combine(services.Environment.GetBaseDirectory(), "agentguard-presence.policy"); its [CallerFilePath] RepoRoot() walk is deleted and the repo has ZERO CallerFilePath hits. It is Linux-gated (under Presence/Linux/) and does not compile on macOS by default; select it with -p:AgentGuardPlatformRid=linux-arm64. It is RED today only because EnvironmentAdapter.GetBaseDirectory() throws.

WHAT REMAINS — YOUR WORK, exactly three things (contract What-to-do steps 2, 3, and 4):

A. EnvironmentAdapter.GetBaseDirectory() => AppContext.BaseDirectory. That is the one class where the raw primitive is legal (AG0011 owner).

B. FakeEnvironment.GetBaseDirectory() implements Decision 5 in FULL, BOTH halves: return the stored base directory, and when it does NOT already end in a directory separator, append exactly one. When it already ends in one, return it UNCHANGED — never doubled to '//'. The separator MUST come from the owned IPlatformFileSystem.DirectorySeparator (src/AgentGuard.Abstractions/Contracts/IPlatformFileSystem.cs:20) per Tim's verbatim mechanism 'bclResult + IPlatformFileSystem.DirectorySeparator' — NEVER a raw Path.DirectorySeparatorChar and NEVER a hardcoded '/'. FakeEnvironment lives in AgentGuard.TestHelpers and is in-memory; it reaches for no System.* member. Note it currently has no access to an IPlatformFileSystem — solving that WITHIN the frozen public seam (for example seeding the separator through the existing private constructor and the Create factory from a value the caller already owns) is your call; if the ONLY way through requires changing a public signature the ARCHITECTURE stage set, STOP and escalate rather than widening it yourself. This normalization must hold on EVERY path including the home-fallback default, which is the shared Fake() harness case at SystemServicesBuilder.cs:247.

C. tests/AgentGuard.CrossPlatform.Tests/AgentGuard.CrossPlatform.Tests.csproj: add the item that copies eng/polkit/agentguard-presence.policy into the test output so it lands in the base directory as agentguard-presence.policy (a <None Include=... CopyToOutputDirectory="PreserveNewest" Link="agentguard-presence.policy" /> item). This is BUILD CONFIG, not a test edit, and it is explicitly yours. You MAY gate it to the Linux leg to match where the test compiles, or copy it unconditionally.

PROOF REQUIRED BEYOND THE STANDARD BRACKET: also run and paste `dotnet test tests/AgentGuard.CrossPlatform.Tests/AgentGuard.CrossPlatform.Tests.csproj -p:AgentGuardPlatformRid=linux-arm64 --filter FullyQualifiedName~PolkitPolicyIntegrityTests` with its exit code, since that is the leg the whole contract exists to fix. If a macOS host cannot execute the Linux-gated impl locally, say so plainly and record that the CI Linux leg is the proving ground — do not fake it.

The Linux-gated file compiled and the test EXECUTED on this macOS host (the read path is managed), so this is a real local pass, not a deferral. CI's Linux leg remains the leg of record for the rest of the Linux suite.

The csproj/props/targets diff is one added <ItemGroup> with a single <None> copy item; no analyzer reference removed, no analyzer opt-out added.

acceptance.evidence: BaseDirectoryAccessorTests.GetBaseDirectory_ReturnsANonEmptyPathToADirectoryThatExists lives directly under tests/AgentGuard.CrossPlatform.Tests/ (not under Presence/, so not per-OS gated) and is inside the 56 passing CrossPlatform.Tests of check 2. It was one of the four RED facts and is now green against the real EnvironmentAdapter.

AgentGuard.CrossPlatform.MacOS` → "PASS per-OS AgentGuard.CrossPlatform.MacOS: 190/215 = 88.37% (min 75%)", GATE_EXIT=0, after the counted-set consistency self-check reported OK. Stale reports were purged before the run (TestResults deleted, full `dotnet test -c Release` re-run) so the gate measured this run, not a mix. Windows is proven on its own CI leg.

acceptance.item: 8. The base directory is separator-terminated in every case (Decision 5), for all three named inputs plus the no-double guard
acceptance.evidence: All four BaseDirectorySeparatorTests facts pass inside check 2: RealBaseDirectory_EndsWithADirectorySeparator (real adapter via SystemServicesBuilder.Real()); FakeBaseDirectory_WhenSeededWithoutATrailingSeparator_AppendsExactlyOne (explicit seed); FakeBaseDirectory_OnTheDefaultHomeFallbackPath_EndsWithADirectorySeparator (the seedless Fake() harness default at SystemServicesBuilder.cs:247 — was failing with "/Users/timothystockstill", now terminated); and FakeBaseDirectory_WhenSeededAlreadyTerminated_ReturnsItUnchangedWithExactlyOneSeparator, the Decision 6 green-by-design guard, which STAYED green — proving the implementation is the tested-then-append form, not an unconditional append. Implementation: FakeEnvironment.GetBaseDirectory() => _baseDirectory.EndsWith(_directorySeparator) ? _baseDirectory : _baseDirectory + _directorySeparator; the separator is the owned IPlatformFileSystem.DirectorySeparator, never a raw Path.DirectorySeparatorChar and never a hardcoded '/'.

walls: NOT A STOP — required disclosure of the one judgment call the orchestrator delegated to me. The contract's Decision 5 requires FakeEnvironment to use the owned IPlatformFileSystem.DirectorySeparator, but FakeEnvironment had no route to one and the ARCHITECTURE-frozen public `Create` signature could not carry it. Every route through Create is closed: the TDD test calls `FakeEnvironment.Create(seed, baseDirectory: seed)` with no separator argument; an optional `char` parameter would need a compile-time default, i.e. a hardcoded '/'; and an `IPlatformFileSystem` parameter on the static `Create` is a build error under AG0031 (a boundary service may not be an ordinary-method parameter). FakeEnvironment also cannot build its own IPlatformFileSystem — ManagedPlatformFileSystem.Create needs an InMemoryFileSystemStore, whose construction AG0027 pins to SystemServicesBuilder. RESOLUTION, taken without widening any frozen signature: SystemServicesBuilder already owns the single once-per-process real-host read (ReadRealHost, the sanctioned SystemServices.Create() door) and already caches plain VALUES from it; I added the separator to that same read — `platform.DirectorySeparator` off the very platform service the existing case-sensitivity probe uses — as a sixth field on the private RealHost record, exposed as `internal static char HostDirectorySeparator`, and FakeEnvironment.Create passes it to the existing PRIVATE constructor. What changed on SystemServicesBuilder is internal-only and private-only; nothing public, and nothing the ARCHITECTURE stage set. FakeEnvironment.Create's public signature is byte-identical to the frozen one. This DOES mean I edited tests/AgentGuard.TestHelpers/SystemServicesBuilder.cs, which the contract's Surfaces list does not name (it names IEnvironment, EnvironmentAdapter, FakeEnvironment, and the test csproj) — flagging it explicitly so the REFUTE panel adjudicates it rather than discovering it. Alternatives I rejected: a second SystemServices.Create() read inside TestHelpers (a straight DRY violation against the existing single host read) and a raw Path.DirectorySeparatorChar in the fake (AG0020 owns that field to the IPlatformFileSystem implementers, and Decision 5 forbids it by name).

NOT A STOP — scope note on the csproj copy item. The contract permits gating the policy copy to the Linux leg or copying it unconditionally; I chose unconditional. Reason: an item with no OS condition cannot drift out of step with the separate Choose/When block that decides where the test compiles, and the copy is inert on the legs that never read the file. Verified the file lands flat in the base directory: ls of tests/AgentGuard.CrossPlatform.Tests/bin/Release/net10.0/agentguard-presence.policy → present, 1554 bytes, identical size to eng/polkit/agentguard-presence.policy.

summary: IMPLEMENT stage: launch the SINGLE fresh worker to implement the behavior against a contract, with rule-, interface-, and test-writing authority ALL revoked. It opens on the build+test bracket, fills the ARCHITECTURE skeleton's NotImplementedException bodies and clears any rule RED until the build is green under the rules AND the RED TDD tests pass, and STOPs at any wall instead of deviating. One worker, not a fan-out (nothing to parallelize). REFUTE is the separate refute.js round the orchestrator runs and loops after this — this script does not self-review.
